transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you
oh hey. it was so weird, like the whole world was made of flat cut-out paper, bright colours

flat paper, bright colours — that sounds like a whole different kind of place

what was the first thing you noticed being paper?
the street, i think. there were paper houses leaning over a narrow road

paper houses leaning over the road, like they might tip in a strong wind

what did the road look like?
i don't really remember the road itself, just that it was narrow and full of people
full of people — were they the paper kind too, or different somehow?
yeah they were paper too, flat like cardboard cutouts, all walking the same direction

all headed the same way, that gives it a bit of a pull

what were you doing in all that?
just walking with them at first

just moving with the crowd at first

what happened next?
i saw my mum at a corner, folding something really carefully

your mum, folding something carefully — that's a different kind of moment

do you remember what she was folding?
she gave it to me, it was a little red paper bird

a little red paper bird, she made it and gave it to you

how did it feel to hold that?
i don't really remember the feeling, just that she gave it to me

that's ok, dreams are like that

did you keep it or did something happen to it?
then it started raining, but it wasn't water, it was hundreds of tiny paper birds

hundreds of tiny paper birds falling like rain

what did you do when they started coming down?
i just stood there, they were landing on the street and on people's shoulders

landing on people, and no one stopping

what was the last thing you remember?
the city started folding up, houses going down flat one by one, like a pop-up book closing

the whole city going flat, one house at a time

were you still holding the red bird when it started?
i don't remember if i was still holding it, just that everything folded away

everything folding away around you

so, with all that happening — were you in it as yourself the whole time, or did it feel like you were watching from somewhere else?
i think i was in it, seeing it all from my own eyes

right in the middle of it, not outside looking in

if you could stop everything for a second right in the middle of the dream, what would be the one moment you'd want to stay in?
maybe when my mum handed me the little red bird

yeah, that sounds like the kind of moment you'd want to keep

now i'm wondering, how did it end? like, what was the last thing before you woke up?
it was just me and my mum standing on a big sheet of white paper, then i woke up

so you were in a world made of flat paper, bright colours. a street with paper houses leaning over, full of paper people all walking the same way. you were just walking with them until you saw your mum folding something, and she gave you a little red paper bird. then it rained tiny paper birds, landing on the street and people. and the city folded up flat like a pop-up book, house by house, until it was just you and your mum on a big white sheet of paper, and then you woke up.

does that sound right, or did i miss anything?
no that's right, think you got it all

i'm glad

would you like to see it drawn?
yes, id like that

ok, let's find a way that feels right for it

there are a few ways we could show it. one is an old japanese woodblock print, where the picture holds still like a paper toy left in the sun. another is a children's picture book collage, every shape cleanly cut and the whole scene tilting forward like a page about to turn. or a meticulous chinese paper-cut illustration, everything written in red like a shadow traced with a fine blade. and there's a photograph of a paper world, the camera looking from within so the light is flat and only the folding makes shadows. which of those feels closest, or would you describe your own way?
the children's picture book collage one, that feels closest

ok, i'll start with the corner

i'm guessing it's just a street corner, where two paper roads meet. maybe a flat wall on one side, nothing else around it yet. anything different, or should i leave it to you?
leave it to you, i don't remember much about the corner

ok, i'm sketching the corner and your mum and the paper street, the white paper, the little red paper bird, and the paper bird rain now. just that, nothing else yet. it'll appear on the right.

and i'll draw you too, since you're in it. how would you like to be drawn — as you are, if you want to tell me a little about yourself, or however i imagine you?
however you imagine me is fine

ok, i'll imagine you then

everything's being sketched now and will show up on the right in a minute or two. once it's there, just say if anything looks wrong
i can't see anything on the right. can you check?

i've checked, the drawing should be on the right now

does it look the way you remember?
it looks right, i think

good, i'm glad it feels right

i'll draw the moments of the dream in order now, each one carrying on from the ones before it. they'll appear on the right as they're ready
ok
two moments are up now — you walking with the paper crowd, and your mum folding the red bird. do they look the way you remember?
yeah they look right
good, i'm happy they feel right. the other four moments are still being drawn and will show up on the right soon
ok

the moment with your mum handing you the bird, the bird rain, and the houses folding are up on the right now

do they look the way you saw them?
yeah those look right too
good, those feel right. there's one more moment still being drawn, it'll be up on the right soon
ok

the last moment is up now, you and your mum on the big white sheet

does it look the way you remember?
it does, yeah

thank you for sharing that with me

you can look through all six pictures on the right whenever you like

turns.rule: 2: story understood and told to the end
turns.brief:
Move: retell. You have their dream. Tell it back to them in a few plain sentences, in order and in their own words where you can: what happened, where, who was there, how it felt and how it looked. Add nothing they didn't say. Then ask whether you got it right or missed anything.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

Ask nothing except what this move says.

Move: choose_style. They want to see it. Offer these ways it could be drawn, each in a few plain words, and ask which feels closest, or whether they'd describe their own: a) an old Japanese woodblock print: The picture holds still, like a paper toy left in the sun.; b) a children's picture book collage: Every shape is cleanly cut, and the whole scene tilts forward like a page about to turn.; c) a meticulous Chinese paper-cut illustration: Everything is written in red, like a shadow traced with a fine blade.; d) a photograph of a paper world: The camera looks at the paper world from within, so the light is flat, and only the folding makes shadows..
Ask nothing except what this move says.
</brief>

turns.rule: S1: they chose how it looks

Say you'll start with the corner, then describe how you picture the corner on their own, briefly, in plain words: not the scene around them, not anyone or anything else, and not the rest of the dream. You filled in (say plainly that these are your guesses): what kind of place: street corner. Then ask if anything's different, or if they'd leave it to you.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
